newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain bank ass'n AEB sees Q3 economic pick-up.
newsitem.headline: Spain bank ass'n AEB sees Q3 economic pick-up.

text.p: Spain's economy is in a recovery phase, helped by greater synchronisation of economic cycles between countries, said the Spanish Banking Association AEB.
"It seems that the slump is over," AEB research director Federico Prades told journalists on Wednesday.

Economic growth will be just above two percent in the third quarter year-on-year, AEB estimates. The latest Bank of Spain monthly report forecast third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth of about two percent.
That would be a slight improvement on the 1.9-percent growth in the second quarter year-on-year, according to the INE National Statistics Institute.
Regarding the public deficit, Prades said "ahead of the results (of the implementation of the 1997 budget, the deficit) should not be substantially far from 4.5 percent of GDP."
The government's target is to get the public deficit down to 4.4 percent of GDP this year.
But 1997's 3.0 percent of GDP target could be affected by social security spending.
"We think the social security budget is more difficult to implement because revenue (forecasts) are overvalued and spending is undervalued," Prades said.
